headline: Up Your Arsenal's PAL v1.00 passes 10% of code on an unusually busy day
summary: Veradictus took Up Your Arsenal's PAL v1.00 decompilation from 8.72% to 10.40% of code, an unusually busy day for this early-stage branch. The project's progress report now counts 6,485 of 16,164 matched functions. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game.
highlights: Batches cover story levels, the multiplayer menu, the front end and boot code. Some implementations adapt Going Commando C where the original games use the same instructions apart from addresses.
Build tools can now retain compiler-generated switch tables and constant pools at their original locations. Padding fixes also let full programs reproduce the original alignment bytes.

Multiplayer levels now use their own global-data base address. Earlier checks could match assembly and C while their names still pointed outside the level, because both checks used the story levels' address.
The final batch reports matching builds for all three PAL core programs and all 49 PAL levels, with the work carried to NTSC-U and all 54 of its build targets matching.
A contributor noticeboard opens in #3 to help avoid duplicate matching work. It does not serve as proof that work is finished.
